entries.reason: a timecode is a frame count, and this release cannot say how many frames a second the media has: no `timecodeStatus` and no `currentTimeline` in the armv7 shared cache of 6.1.3 (568965 names, armv7), and the port's own transport bar formats elapsed and remaining time from the player's CMTime without ever needing a frame rate. Any HH:MM:SS:FF this port drew would carry a frame rate nobody measured, which is the invented value the registry is for. Apple's own property is documented to show a timecode only "if available", and what is unavailable here is the frame rate, not the intent

entries.reason: the property asks for picture-in-picture to start as the application leaves the foreground, and this port's picture-in-picture cannot do that: its window is a UIWindow the application owns, so it is suspended with the rest of the application when the application is not running, exactly as the facts for AVPictureInPictureController record. Answering YES would be a promise the port cannot keep - and answering NO would be false, because starting on the way out is precisely what this port cannot do, so neither value would be the truth

entries.reason: the flag is for a system service that samples decoded frames for analysis, and this port has no such consumer: it draws the frames itself, through its own CADisplayLink reading AVPlayerItemVideoOutput (AVPlayerViewController.m's -charon_drawFrame: and +keyPathsForValuesAffectingReadyForDisplay). The release carries no frame-analysis surface either - allowsVideoFrameAnalysis, videoFrameAnalysis, analyzeVideoFrame, AVVideoFrameAnalysis and requestVideoFrameAnalysis are all absent from the armv7 cache of 6.1.3 - so there is nothing on the other side of the flag for it to allow
